intro: Beverly Hills does the classics well: power-lunch rooms, old Hollywood martinis, serious omakase and some of the best sandwiches in LA. Between meals there are mansions, gardens and galleries within a few blocks of Rodeo.

places.w: A classic deli with an eclectic, very Beverly Hills crowd.
places.o: Bagel and lox, stuffed cabbage and matzah ball soup.

places.n: The Cheese Store of Beverly Hills
places.w: A fromagerie open for more than 50 years that makes some of the best deli sandwiches in LA.
places.o: La Zucca or The Dom.

places.w: Giant Italian focaccia sandwiches for a fast lunch. Seating is a small sidewalk area.
places.o: The prosciutto focaccia.

places.w: A kosher Israeli counter with big portions and real value for Beverly Hills.
places.o: A plate with shawarma, schnitzel or falafel.

places.w: An upscale soba shop with chewy house-made noodles and a rich broth.
places.o: The #1 bowl.

places.w: The iconic LA dining room, with attentive service and a big-night feel.
places.o: Smoked salmon pizza and spicy tuna cones.

places.w: A three-level pasta palace with reliably excellent handmade pasta. The rooftop bar is walk-in only.
places.o: Any flour-and-egg pasta and a tomato martini. Reservations drop 7 days out at 9am.

places.w: An old Hollywood red-sauce room with strong martinis and real glamour.
places.o: Bone-in veal parm, tableside Caesar and a martini.

places.w: A grand, people-watching room that makes an ordinary dinner feel ritzy. Weekend waits can hit two hours.
places.o: Barbecue ribs, spinach-artichoke dip or the French dip.

places.w: A showbiz power-lunch classic known for polished, professional service.
places.o: Chicken piccata, the chopped salad and brownie à la mode.

places.w: A neighborhood-style Italian that suits big family and friend groups.
places.o: Pappardelle, tuna carpaccio and ossobuco.

places.w: Seafood-focused Italian that's consistently good and sometimes great, in a big room full of business dinners.
places.o: Lobster and burrata, and the octopus and bone marrow fusilli.

places.w: A wagyu prix fixe that's real value for premium beef, at $87 for five courses.
places.o: The five-course menu.

places.w: A Beverly Hills rite of passage since long before the chain spread.
places.o: Prime rib and the spinning salad.

places.w: Nobu Matsuhisa's original, home of the yellowtail jalapeño, served without pretension.
places.o: The omakase, or the signature dishes.

places.w: A hidden four-seat counter that critics say makes the best nigiri in Beverly Hills.
places.o: The 20-course omakase, about $220.

places.w: An omakase room tucked behind Sugarfish, with two 10-person seatings a night.
places.o: The 22-course omakase. Arrive on time and don't ask for changes.

places.n: Polo Lounge at the Beverly Hills Hotel
places.w: The pink hotel's famous lounge, worth a visit even if you aren't staying.
places.o: A drink or brunch on the patio.

places.a: Santa Monica Blvd near Canon Dr
places.w: A long, tree-lined park with the Beverly Hills sign everyone photographs.
places.o: The Beverly Hills Art Show runs here in May and October.

places.w: The luxury shopping street, including Two Rodeo and Anderson Court.
places.o: Window-shop, then lunch at The Cheese Store a few blocks over.

places.w: A 55-room Tudor estate whose gardens and grounds are free to walk.
places.o: The interior opens only for events and tours.

places.w: A lavish 1911 estate with formal gardens and a mansion.
places.o: Docent-led tours only, booked in advance.

places.w: The storybook 1921 'Witch's House.' You can't go in, but it's worth the detour.
places.o: Busiest around Halloween.

places.w: Exhibitions from major contemporary artists in a gallery a block off Rodeo.
places.o: Check what's showing before you go.

places.w: A gallery for emerging artists in a space designed by Ai Weiwei.
places.o: Pair it with the Wallis next door.

places.w: A performing arts center in a converted 1933 post office, booking everything from jazz to comedy.
places.o: Check the Goldsmith Theater lineup.

places.w: A bright corner cafe that has become the Beverly Hills breakfast burrito spot. The kitchen cooks without seed oils, and the matcha menu is as big a draw as the coffee.
places.o: The Faregrounds breakfast burrito with a strawberry matcha. Open weekdays from 7 a.m.; closed on weekends.

places.n: Fountain Coffee Room at the Beverly Hills Hotel
places.w: A pink, 1949 soda-fountain counter inside the Beverly Hills Hotel with about 20 stools and breakfast served all day. It is walk-in only, so you sit at the counter and watch the room.
places.o: Silver dollar pancakes and a milkshake. Daily, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.

places.n: THE Blvd at the Beverly Wilshire
places.w: The Beverly Wilshire's street-level dining room, looking straight down Rodeo Drive. A polished Four Seasons breakfast and a classic spot for a morning meeting.
places.o: A window table at the start of the day, then a walk up Rodeo.

places.n: The Rooftop at the Waldorf Astoria
places.w: A garden-style rooftop 12 floors above Beverly Hills with one of the widest views in the city. It is the see-and-be-seen sunset drink in town, and the prices match.
places.o: Walk in for the bar and lounge around sunset; book ahead if you want a table.
